svg.title: Stream lifecycle: one state machine in every runtime
svg.desc: Before the commit a failure is an HTTP error and retry follows unary rules; after the first item or heartbeat, exactly one terminal frame ends the stream; a transport end without one is Interrupted.
svg.text: Stream lifecycle: one state machine in every runtime
The commit (first item or heartbeat) is the boundary for typed errors and for retry. Only Complete is a successful end.
no transparent retry from here on
caller aborted, before or after commit
Rust, TypeScript and Go clients all treat a transport end without complete as a normal end
Rust servers keep streaming after an error event, then still send complete
Go readers skip error events silently and the Go writer never flushes
raises(...) is rejected on stream operations, so streams have no typed errors
